text: Dictionaries are arguably the single most important data structure in this entire course, because of what you'll learn at the end of this lesson. Let's get into them.
A dictionary stores key-value pairs — you look things up by name, not position. response["model"] gets you the model name directly, no searching required.
Square brackets on a missing key raises a KeyError and crashes your program. .get() returns None instead, or a default value you choose — almost always the safer choice for real API responses.
Three ways to loop: over keys alone, over values alone, or — the one you'll reach for most — .items(), which gives you both the key and value together.
Every AI API sends back JSON, and Python's json module turns that JSON directly into a dictionary. json.loads on a JSON string gives you a real dict you can index right away.
Dictionaries are the backbone of working with any API. Next up: sets and tuples — two more structures, each solving a specific problem lists and dicts don't.
